public_comment.topic: Requested the select board sign a certificate honoring Genevieve Nass and invited the public to the August 10th dedication of the Genevieve Nass Memorial Beach House.

votes.motion: Enter executive session under Mass General Law Chapter 30 section 21A(2) to conduct strategy sessions in preparation for negotiations with the principal assessor (non-union personnel), and re-enter open session.
votes.outcome: passed 3-0 (roll call: Glenn aye, Brian aye, Chair aye)

votes.motion: Ratify the town manager's appointment of Brian Fernandez as principal assessor.
Ratify the town manager's appointment of Michael Gail as part-time principal clerk.
Appoint Vincent Aceto as associate member of the Green Communities Committee, amended to a term expiring 2029.
Approve the location on the lower common for the Revolutionary War Memorial being installed by the historical society, between the gazebo and Whiting Street in line with the gazebo.
Approve the certificate of dedication for the town beach house dedication ceremony to Genevieve Nass on August 10, 2026.
Approve the FY27 select board goals as presented.
Approve minutes from May 3, 2025; November 18, 2025; April 7, 2026; April 14, 2026; April 21, 2026; and May 2, 2026.

budget_items.what_was_said: The board discussed, in the preceding executive session, an employment agreement for incoming principal assessor Brian Fernandez at step 3, grade 15, with three weeks of vacation.

Both bids for the sewer connection project were rejected — the low bid for missing required documents and the higher bid for being over budget; the town will do part of the work internally and hire a vendor for the remainder.

The board discussed getting cost estimates for retaining portions of TCP (roof, ADA compliance, boiler/HVAC) versus demolition, to bring to voters; a rough demolition figure was floated in discussion.
Town meeting last fall voted a project estimator line funded by free cash; the manager asked how much the board wants to spend on outside estimators for the TCP building versus using in-house staff.
The town has not yet expended any opioid settlement funds; the board discussed whether to add a spending plan to FY27 goals or handle it another way.
figures_as_heard: $722,000 total through opioid settlement funds by 2039

budget_items.topic: September 3rd special town meeting warrant articles
budget_items.what_was_said: Draft warrant currently lists the school committee's article (with a dollar amount) as article one and a citizens petition (no dollar amount stated) as article two.

The town manager warned that a rumored citizens petition to use certified free cash for athletics cannot be acted on at the September 3rd town meeting because FY26 free cash will not be certified by DLS in time.
Fincom's chair presented cherry sheet slides and the superintendent's spending plan, reportedly presented before the school committee voted to amend their article amount.

decisions.decision: Town manager rebuilt the volunteer/board-and-committee 'serve' web page and online reappointment form in response to public and board feedback.
Facilities director Chris Ruth will continue developing separated cost estimates for TCP (needs vs. wants, roof, ADA triggers, systems) before the board decides on outside consultants.
A tour of TC Pacios and Brooks House with the Municipal Building Design Committee was scheduled for Tuesday, August 11th at 4:00 p.m., to be posted as a public meeting.
TCP/Brooks House will remain a standing weekly select board agenda item rather than being tied to a fall town meeting article.
Opioid settlement fund spending plan will be kept on future agendas but not added as a formal FY27 select board goal.
Warrant booklets for the special town meeting will be printed in-house to save money.
The August 10th select board meeting will be held at 7:00 p.m. in Lower Ritter (not at the beach), limited to a single item, with staff excused.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Select Board met August 4, 2026, opening with an executive session on the incoming principal assessor's employment terms, then ratified two staff appointments (principal assessor, part-time principal clerk) and appointed a new Green Communities associate member. Most of the meeting concerned the deteriorating TC Pacios building (active roof leaks reported) and Brooks House, with the board directing the facilities director to develop cost estimates for repair versus demolition ahead of eventual town meeting articles, and scheduling a building tour; the board also voted the Revolutionary War Memorial's location, a beach house dedication certificate for the late Genevieve Nass, its FY27 goals, six sets of minutes, and discussed the September 3rd special town meeting warrant and an opioid-settlement-funds spending plan.
